steps.body: You can count forward from ANY starting number, not just a round one — just repeat the same jump size the right number of times.
Hop it, then name the total move.

commonLandings.feedback: You counted by 1s — each hop is a TEN: 450 → 460 → 470 → 480.
That's 2 hops. Three hops of ten: one more to 480.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop adds a full ten: 450 → 460 → 470 → 480.

predict.prompt: 3 hops of 10 from 450 — how far from 450 will you end up in total?
predict.reveal: 3 hops of 10 cover 3 × 10 = 30, so you land on 480 — counting forward by tens is really adding one 30 in a single thought. 13 mixes up the hop size with the hop count.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents count forward.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for count forward must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines count forward.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

steps.body: Count forward by hundreds, several jumps.
explanationVariants: Each jump adds the same skip amount.

widget.prompt: Count forward from 230 by 100s, 2 times. What number do you land on?

commonErrors.feedback: Each jump adds 100, not 1. Two jumps of 100 from 230: 230+200=430.
That's 2 jumps of 10, not 100. Two jumps of 100 from 230 is 430.

steps.body: Count forward by fives, several jumps — the same repeated-addition idea, just with a smaller step.
Count the jumps instead of the landing number.

widget.prompt: Starting at 615, you take jumps of 5: 620, 625, 630, 635. How many jumps did you take?

commonErrors.feedback: 635 is the landing number, not the count of jumps. Listed are 4 stops: 620, 625, 630, 635 — that's 4 jumps.
5 is the size of each jump, not how many jumps happened. Counting the stops listed gives 4 jumps.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Four stops are listed after 615 — 620, 625, 630, 635 — so that's 4 jumps.

steps.body: This is just skip-counting stretched out — instead of finding the very next number, you find the number several jumps later.
Count backward this time, crossing a rollover.

widget.prompt: Count backward from 480 by 10s, 3 times. What number do you land on?

commonErrors.feedback: Each jump subtracts 10, not 1. Three jumps of 10 back from 480: 480−30=450.
That's 3 jumps of 100, not 10. Three jumps of 10 back from 480 is 450.

steps.body: Work backward to find the starting number.
explanationVariants: Work backward from the landing number to find the start.

widget.prompt: After counting forward by 100s, 3 times, you land on 600. Where did you start?

commonErrors.feedback: That adds the jumps instead of working backward. Undo three jumps of 100 from 600: 600−300=300.
That subtracts 1 each time instead of 100. Undoing three jumps of 100 from 600 gives 300.

steps.body: Work out the size of each jump.
explanationVariants: The total distance is 205 − 190 = 15, split evenly across 3 jumps: 5 each.
Find the total distance, then split it evenly across the jumps.

widget.prompt: Counting forward from 190, three equal jumps land on 205. How big was each jump?

commonErrors.feedback: 15 is the total distance covered in three jumps, not the size of one jump. 15 ÷ 3 = 5.
3 is how many jumps were taken, not how big each one was. Each jump was 5.

widget.fallbackFeedback: The total distance is 205 − 190 = 15, split evenly across 3 jumps: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 each.

explanationVariants: 760 + 10×5 = 810 — Kai added only the jump count, not the total distance.
Multiply jump size by number of jumps, then add to the start.

widget.prompt: Kai started at 760 and took 5 jumps of 10, but said he landed on 765. What is the correct landing number?

commonErrors.feedback: That repeats Kai's mistake of adding just the number of jumps (5) instead of 5 jumps of 10. The correct total is 760+50=810.
That's 5 jumps of 100, not 10. Five jumps of 10 from 760 is 810.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Five jumps of 10 add up to 50: 760 + 50 = 810.

hints: Each jump adds 10, and there are 5 jumps — that's 5×10=50 total, not just 5.
Kai's mistake was adding the jump COUNT instead of the total distance covered.

steps.body: Counting forward several jumps just repeats the same skip amount, starting from anywhere — even across a hundred-rollover.
takeaways: Count forward N times means adding the skip amount N times.
The starting number can be anything, not just a round number.
The process crosses hundred-rollovers the same way it works anywhere else.
steps.teaser: you've completed place value structure and counting to 1000 — more of this course is still ahead.

concept.body: Counting forward several times means repeating the same jump size that many times. From 450, three jumps of 10: 450+10+10+10=480.

widget.prompt: Count forward from 450 by 10s, 3 times. What number do you land on?

commonErrors.feedback: You counted by 100s. Three tens from 450: 460, 470, 480.
